title: Nocturne upload never runs: NocturneUploader constructor always throws
body:
Nocturne upload never runs. Once you have authenticated, every upload attempt throws inside the `NocturneUploader` constructor and the exception is swallowed. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is shown in the UI.

Found on `master` at `f30226459`, from #4529.

### What happens

`NocturneUploader`'s constructor ends with:

```java
// NocturneUploader.java:110
apiClient.setAccessToken(accessToken);
```

In `nocturne-java` 0.2.4 that method has no body other than a throw:

```
public void setAccessToken(java.lang.String);
   0: new    // class java/lang/RuntimeException
   4: ldc    // String No OAuth2 authentication configured!
   9: athrow
```

No condition, no early return. `ApiClient.init()` leaves `authentications` an empty map, so there is no auth scheme to set a token on. `HttpBearerAuth` ships in the jar but is never registered.

`UploaderTask.java:180` constructs the uploader inside a `try` whose `catch (Exception e)` logs and returns, so the throw never surfaces:

```java
final NocturneUploader nocturneUploader = new NocturneUploader(xdrip.getAppContext());
```

### Who this affects

Only users who have actually completed the device flow. Without a token, `getValidAccessToken()` returns null and the constructor takes the early return at `NocturneUploader.java:96` with a log line. With a valid token it goes on to line 110 and throws. So the failure is invisible in exactly the case where upload is supposed to work.

`NocturneOAuthService` is unaffected — it never calls `setAccessToken`, which is why registration and the device flow work.

### Notes

The `ApiClient` surface that does work is `addDefaultHeader`, already used two lines above for `Origin`.

Unrelated to okhttp — measured at 4.12.0. Turned up while writing test coverage for the HTTP paths (#4699): the planned test could not construct the uploader at all.
